# DirectX models


`LoadMesh`, `LoadAnimMesh` and `LoadAnimSeq` read DirectX `.x` files as the original does, in all three kinds: text (`xof 0303txt 0032`), binary (`bin `, with 32 or 64 bit floats) and compressed (`tzip` for text and `bzip` for binary, in MSZip blocks). The file type is told by what is in the file, not by its name. The templates of Direct3D (`Mesh`, `Frame`, `Material`, `AnimationSet` and so on) are known, templates in the file are added to them, and objects that have no template are skipped.

* A `Frame` is an entity (a mesh entity, as in the original) with the name of the frame. Its `FrameTransformMatrix` becomes its position, scale and rotation; a skew in the matrix is lost. A `Mesh` outside of any frame belongs to the entity at the top.
* `LoadMesh` makes one mesh of all frames as they are before the animation, `LoadAnimMesh` keeps every frame as an entity.
* A mesh has its vertices, faces (a face of more corners than three is split into a fan), normals, one set of texture coordinates and vertex colors (set on the vertices; `EntityFX` 2 shows them, as with any mesh). A mesh without normals gets them made. A mesh with `MeshNormals` or `MeshTextureCoords` for a different number of vertices than it has uses neither, as in the original.
* The materials of `MeshMaterialList` become brushes: the face color (a color alpha of 0 counts as opaque, as in the original), and the first `TextureFilename`, which also makes the color white. The picture is looked for next to the model, and then in the folder of the program; folders from the machine that made the model are cut off. Triangles with the same brush share a surface.
* The animation sets are the animation: for each `Animation` the keys (rotation, scale, position, in frames) are put on the frame that the animation names. The rotation is the quaternion of the file as it is, scales are made positive, matrix keys (type 4) are not used. The animation is as long as the last key. All animation sets are one animation, as in the original.
* There are no bones: `XSkinMeshHeader` and `SkinWeights` are read but not used, so a mesh moves with its frame, as in the original.
* `LoaderMatrix "x", ...` turns the vertices, normals, frames and keys of every `.x` file that is loaded after it.
